summary: Flat-roofed log cabin on the Challis National Forest, dated to 1940; its planned L-4 cab was never finished and it was destroyed in 2000.

facts.design: Flat-roofed log cabin; planned L-4 cab never completed
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 2000 before its planned L-4 cab was finished.

events.note: Flat-roofed log cabin. Forest Lookouts gives only the 1940s.
Both pages give 2000. No cause is given in the pages read.

evidence.supports: 17 miles NNW of Challis, Challis National Forest
on the edge of Frank Church wilderness; flat-roofed log cabin built 1940
evidence.quote: Bordering the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness, this flat-roofed log cabin, built in 1940,

evidence.supports: dated only to the 1940s; log cabin never completed
planned L-4 cab on top, never completed
evidence.quote: was scheduled to have an L-4 cab added on top. It was never completed, and was eventually destroyed in 2000.

evidence.supports: planned L-4 cab on top, never completed
evidence.quote: The flat-roofed cabin was scheduled to have an L-4 cab added to the top, but it was never completed before being destroyed in 2000.

corrections.why: Both pages describe a flat-roofed log cabin whose planned L-4 cab was never built, so no tower was completed. The FFLA list gives the type as Log base.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives only the 1940s. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1940, so 1940 is used.

notes_for_editor: Elevation 9,421 ft (about 2,871 m) appears on two pages; elevation_m is null in the record. Only three pages support the story, and one web search found no independent source. Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com both credit the Fire Lookout Museum for their photos, so they may share an origin. Forest Lookouts cites Kresek for its date. The Idaho Fire Lookouts photo already in the record was not re-checked. Corrections are proposed only: kind tower to unknown.
